claims.text: Machine-learning-guided optimization of fused-slurry processing parameters can reliably produce a dual-layer protective scale on refractory high-entropy alloys.
A fused-slurry silicide coating can improve the high-temperature oxidation resistance of a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Refractory high-entropy alloy substrates are inherently susceptible to oxidation at high temperatures.
The fused-slurry method can deposit a Si-20Cr-20Fe coating on a refractory high-entropy alloy.
A machine-learning framework can optimize the slurry composition, processing temperature, and processing time for this coating system.
The proposed oxidation-resistance benefit applies at temperatures up to approximately 1300 °C.
The proposed benefit applies under controlled atmospheric conditions.
The initial silicide coating has an outer high-silicon layer mainly composed of MSi2.
The initial silicide coating has an inner low-silicon layer mainly containing M5Si3.
After oxidation, the coating consists of an outer oxide layer and an inner silicide layer.
The oxide-silicide scale formed after oxidation is tightly adherent.
Silicon diffuses from the silicide coating into the refractory high-entropy alloy substrate during high-temperature oxidation.
Machine-learning optimization identifies processing regimes that promote uniform coating deposition.
Machine-learning optimization produces controlled silicon diffusion.
The oxide layer and underlying silicide retard oxidation by minimizing oxygen ingress.
The oxide-silicide structure improves protective-scale adhesion.
ML-optimized coatings will have significantly lower oxidation rates than coatings produced using conventional trial-and-error parameters.
ML-optimized coatings will show improved scale stability relative to conventionally processed coatings.
Coatings produced using standard non-data-driven parameters typically have higher oxidation rates and less uniform protective scales.
The magnitude of the benefit may vary with alloy composition and environmental conditions.
